newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Minor grain loss seen in west Ukraine from floods.
newsitem.headline: Minor grain loss seen in west Ukraine from floods.

text.p: Ukraine suffered only minor grain losses in western regions near the Polish border after recent rains left 50 towns and villages under water, an agricultural expert said on Tuesday.
"Only small areas were damaged," Olexander Kotyash, chief agronomist of the Lviv regional administration, told Reuters by telephone.
"This year our plan for the Lviv region was to produce 600,000 tonnes of grain, so we may lose about 60,000 tonnes," he said.
Ukraine has forecast net grain output of up to 37 million tonnes this year, compared with a poor 25.4 million tonnes last year blamed on drought early in the growing season.
Kotyash said 44,000 hectares, one-tenth of areas sown mostly to wheat, were damaged by flooding, heavy rains or hail that hit the region at the weekend.
Most of Ukraine's grain is grown in central and southern regions and away from the hilly western areas.
Harvesting has started in most regions.
Kotyash said the sun was shining and was forecast to keep shining for the next several days.
"We think this is probably the end of rains," he said.
He added there was no sunseed and only small amounts of sugar beets growing in the areas hit by rains and flooding.
Ukraine's forecasts call for about 2.5 million tonnes of sunflower seed this year against 2.04 million tonnes in 1996, and 27 million tonnes of sugar beet compared with 24 million tonnes last year.
